core_obligations: Upgrade the pairing hypothesis to absolute pseudo-coherence.
Run the duality computation against a generator.
Conclude fibre boundedness and invoke the criterion.
difficulty_reason: For A a ring, X flat separated of finite presentation over A and K in D_QCoh(O_X): if RGamma(X, E (x) K) is perfect in D(A) for every perfect E, then K is Spec(A)-perfect. The retained proof is complete: first upgrade K to absolute pseudo-coherence — the improved variant of the pairing lemma (chapter lemma characterize-pcoherent-improved, in the revived queue) gives relative pseudo-coherence and the moot lemma (card L16171) converts it to absolute; the bounded-below detection proposition puts K in D^-(O_X). Fibrewise: for every prime p of A, the bounded-on-fibres criterion (card L16169) reduces perfection to Li^*K bounded below on the fibre Y over p; a Bondal-van den Bergh generator G of D_QCoh(O_X) (theorem bondal-van-den-Bergh) has its restriction Li^*G generating D_QCoh(O_Y) (remark pullback-generator), and the displayed duality computation — RHom_Y(Li^*G, Li^*K) = RGamma(X, G^vee (x) K) (x)_A k(p), justified by the dual-perfect-complex lemma and the compare-base-change lemma using flatness — is perfect over k(p) by hypothesis; the bounded-below detection proposition applied on the fibre concludes. Retained author proof at lines 12789-12829.
